source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-69: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 69 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
For Mooncake variant 69, treat disaggregated KV serving as an environment-dependent hypothesis, not a guaranteed improvement. Assume a multi-node long-context service, but first record model and runtime versions, GPU/NIC models, PCIe/NUMA affinity, link rate, memory limits, failure domains, prompt and generation-length distributions, concurrency, batching, and tenant authorization boundaries. Do not invent platform facts; unknowns must remain explicit.

Specify component ownership, placement, replication, lifecycle, and the control-plane state transitions before enabling remote reuse. Separate prefill workers, which construct KV, from decode workers, which consume it. Define the KV block format and precision, ownership and placement, replication, TTL/eviction priority, cache-key isolation, version/checksum validation, admission quotas, batching, migration, and control-plane behavior. Reject stale, partial, unauthorized, or checksum-failing blocks. On a miss, transfer failure, node loss, or control-plane inconsistency, use a bounded local/recompute fallback; never silently use unverified data. Preserve tenant isolation and rate limits during fallback.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at a preregistered offered load and fixed prompt/output mix, remote KV reduces decode time-to-first-token or HBM pressure without increasing p95/p99 latency, error rate, or cross-tenant risk beyond stated thresholds versus (a) local KV and (b) a conventional matched distributed baseline. Measure TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, hit/miss rate, bytes transferred, RDMA retries, CPU/GPU utilization, HBM usage, evictions, queueing, errors, and recovery time with units and synchronized timestamps. Repeat across context lengths and concurrency; report uncertainty and separate warm/cold cache cases. Control for model/kernel versions, batching, placement, compression, background traffic, and admission policy.

Failure/rollback gate: disable remote reuse and drain or quarantine affected blocks if checksums or versions fail, RDMA/link errors or stale metadata exceed the predeclared limit, p99 latency or error rate breaches the SLO, or isolation/audit checks fail. Roll back to the last known-good local/recompute path and retain audit logs. Evidence required before claiming improvement includes topology and configuration inventory, raw per-request traces/counters, matched-baseline results, failure-injection results for cache corruption, link/node/control-plane loss, and an independent review of authorization and tenant isolation.
risks: Actual Mooncake implementation details, transport behavior, and performance depend on versions, topology, workload, and configuration not supplied by the prompt.
Remote KV can amplify stale-data, cache-poisoning, tenant-isolation, bandwidth, and tail-latency risks if validation or admission controls are incomplete.

Matched local and conventional distributed baselines with synchronized per-request metrics and uncertainty.
Fault-injection and recovery results for stale/corrupt KV, RDMA/link loss, node loss, and control-plane inconsistency.

corrected_answer:
For Mooncake variant 78, treat disaggregated KV serving as an environment-dependent hypothesis, not a guaranteed improvement. Assume a multi-node long-context service, but first record model and runtime versions, GPU/NIC models, PCIe/NUMA affinity, link rate, memory limits, failure domains, prompt and generation-length distributions, concurrency, batching, and tenant authorization boundaries. Do not invent platform facts; unknowns must remain explicit.

Use a preregistered workload and matched baselines to attribute any gain rather than treating lower end-to-end time as proof of a cache benefit. Separate prefill workers, which construct KV, from decode workers, which consume it. Define the KV block format and precision, ownership and placement, replication, TTL/eviction priority, cache-key isolation, version/checksum validation, admission quotas, batching, migration, and control-plane behavior. Reject stale, partial, unauthorized, or checksum-failing blocks. On a miss, transfer failure, node loss, or control-plane inconsistency, use a bounded local/recompute fallback; never silently use unverified data. Preserve tenant isolation and rate limits during fallback.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at a preregistered offered load and fixed prompt/output mix, remote KV reduces decode time-to-first-token or HBM pressure without increasing p95/p99 latency, error rate, or cross-tenant risk beyond stated thresholds versus (a) local KV and (b) a conventional matched distributed baseline. Measure TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, hit/miss rate, bytes transferred, RDMA retries, CPU/GPU utilization, HBM usage, evictions, queueing, errors, and recovery time with units and synchronized timestamps. Repeat across context lengths and concurrency; report uncertainty and separate warm/cold cache cases. Control for model/kernel versions, batching, placement, compression, background traffic, and admission policy.

Failure/rollback gate: disable remote reuse and drain or quarantine affected blocks if checksums or versions fail, RDMA/link errors or stale metadata exceed the predeclared limit, p99 latency or error rate breaches the SLO, or isolation/audit checks fail. Roll back to the last known-good local/recompute path and retain audit logs. Evidence required before claiming improvement includes topology and configuration inventory, raw per-request traces/counters, matched-baseline results, failure-injection results for cache corruption, link/node/control-plane loss, and an independent review of authorization and tenant isolation.
risks: Actual Mooncake implementation details, transport behavior, and performance depend on versions, topology, workload, and configuration not supplied by the prompt.
Remote KV can amplify stale-data, cache-poisoning, tenant-isolation, bandwidth, and tail-latency risks if validation or admission controls are incomplete.

Matched local and conventional distributed baselines with synchronized per-request metrics and uncertainty.
